title: Network
description: Shows your Wi-Fi or cable connection: network name, signal and speed.

placeholders.description: The network card name, like wlan0.
The default gateway for the interface
The subnetmask corresponding to the IP(V4).
The subnetmask corresponding to the IP(V6).
The subnetmask corresponding to the IP(V4) in CIDR notation.
The subnetmask corresponding to the IP(V6) in CIDR notation.
MAC address (BSSID) of the wireless access point.
Signal strength of the wireless network in dBm.
Instant up speed in bytes/seconds, formatted compactly (e.g. 1.2K).
Instant down speed in bytes/seconds, formatted compactly (e.g. 1.2K).
An icon from "Icons" that matches the signal.

interface.label: Network card
interface.doc: Use the defined interface instead of auto-detection. Accepts wildcard.
interface.description: Use a specific network card (like wlan0) instead of choosing one automatically. You can use * as a wildcard, like wl*.

rfkill.label: Detect when Wi-Fi is switched off
rfkill.doc: If enabled, the disabled format will be used when rfkill is blocking wlan interfaces.
rfkill.description: Use the "turned off" text when Wi-Fi is disabled, for example in airplane mode.

interval.label: Refresh every
interval.doc: The interval in which the network information gets polled (e.g. signal strength).
interval.description: How often the signal strength and speed are updated. Use a small value, like 2, if you show the speed.

family.label: Address type
family.doc: The address family that is used for the format replacement {ipaddr} and to determine if a network connection is present. Set it to ipv4_6 to display both.
family.description: Which kind of IP address {ipaddr} shows.

format.label: What to show
format.doc: The format, how information should be displayed. This format is used when other formats aren't specified.
format.description: The default text, used when no more specific text below is set.

format-ethernet.label: What to show on cable
format-ethernet.doc: This format is used when an ethernet interface is displayed.
format-ethernet.description: This format is used when an ethernet interface is displayed.

format-wifi.label: What to show on Wi-Fi
format-wifi.doc: This format is used when a wireless interface is displayed.
format-wifi.description: For example "{icon} {essid}" shows an icon and the network name.

format-linked.label: What to show when connected without an address
format-linked.doc: This format is used when a linked interface with no IP address is displayed.
format-linked.description: The cable or Wi-Fi is connected, but you have no IP address yet.

format-disconnected.label: What to show when disconnected
format-disconnected.doc: This format is used when the displayed interface is disconnected.
format-disconnected.description: This format is used when the displayed interface is disconnected.

format-disabled.label: What to show when Wi-Fi is off
format-disabled.doc: This format is used when rfkill is blocking wlan interfaces.
format-disabled.description: This format is used when rfkill is blocking wlan interfaces.

format-alt.label: What to show after a click
format-alt.doc: On click, toggle between this format and the regular format. The click button is set with format-alt-click (defaults to the left button).
format-alt.description: Clicking the module switches to this text. Click again to go back.

format-icons.label: Icons
format-icons.doc: Based on the current signal strength, the corresponding icon gets selected. The order is low to high. Or by the state if it is an object.
format-icons.description: Icons for {icon}, from weak to strong signal.

rotate.label: Rotation
rotate.doc: Positive value to rotate the text label (in 90 degree increments).
rotate.description: Rotate the text. Mostly useful on vertical bars.

max-length.label: Maximum length
max-length.doc: The maximum length in character the module should display.
max-length.description: Cut the text when it is longer than this. Empty means no limit.

min-length.label: Minimum length
min-length.doc: The minimum length in characters the module should accept.
min-length.description: Keep the module at least this wide, so the bar doesn't jump around when the text changes.

align.label: Text position
align.doc: The alignment of the label within the module, where 0 is left-aligned and 1 is right-aligned. If the module is rotated, it will follow the flow of the text.
align.description: Where the text sits inside the module: 0 is left, 0.5 is center, 1 is right.

justify.label: Line alignment
justify.doc: The alignment of the text within the module's label, allowing options 'left', 'right', or 'center' to define the positioning.
justify.description: How lines are aligned when the text has more than one line.

on-click.label: Left click runs
on-click.doc: Command to execute when clicked on the module.
on-click.description: A command to run when you click the module. Empty keeps the normal behavior.

on-click-middle.label: Middle click runs
on-click-middle.doc: Command to execute when middle-clicked on the module using mousewheel.
on-click-middle.description: A command to run when you click the module with the mouse wheel.

on-click-right.label: Right click runs
on-click-right.doc: Command to execute when you right-click on the module.
on-click-right.description: A command to run when you right-click the module.

on-update.label: On every refresh run
on-update.doc: Command to execute when the module is updated.
on-update.description: A command to run each time the module updates.

on-scroll-up.label: Scroll up runs
on-scroll-up.doc: Command to execute when scrolling up on the module.
on-scroll-up.description: A command to run when you scroll up over the module. It replaces what scrolling normally does.

on-scroll-down.label: Scroll down runs
on-scroll-down.doc: Command to execute when scrolling down on the module.
on-scroll-down.description: A command to run when you scroll down over the module. It replaces what scrolling normally does.

smooth-scrolling-threshold.label: Scroll sensitivity
smooth-scrolling-threshold.doc: Threshold to be used when scrolling.
smooth-scrolling-threshold.description: How far you must scroll on a touchpad before something happens. Higher means less sensitive.

tooltip.label: Show tooltip
tooltip.doc: Option to disable tooltip on hover.
tooltip.description: Show a small popup with more details when the mouse is over the module.

tooltip-format.label: Tooltip text
tooltip-format.doc: The format, how information should be displayed in the tooltip. This format is used when other formats aren't specified.
tooltip-format.description: What the popup shows. It uses the same placeholders as the bar text.

tooltip-format-ethernet.label: Tooltip on cable
tooltip-format-ethernet.doc: This format is used when an ethernet interface is displayed.
tooltip-format-ethernet.description: This format is used when an ethernet interface is displayed.

tooltip-format-wifi.label: Tooltip on Wi-Fi
tooltip-format-wifi.doc: This format is used when a wireless interface is displayed.
tooltip-format-wifi.description: This format is used when a wireless interface is displayed.

tooltip-format-disconnected.label: Tooltip when disconnected
tooltip-format-disconnected.doc: This format is used when the displayed interface is disconnected.
tooltip-format-disconnected.description: This format is used when the displayed interface is disconnected.

tooltip-format-disabled.label: Tooltip when Wi-Fi is off
tooltip-format-disabled.doc: This format is used when rfkill is blocking wlan interfaces.
tooltip-format-disabled.description: This format is used when rfkill is blocking wlan interfaces.

menu.label: Open popup menu with
menu.description: Which click opens a popup menu for this module.

menu-file.label: Menu layout file
menu-file.doc: Location of the menu descriptor file. There need to be an element of type GtkMenu with id menu
menu-file.description: The file that describes the menu entries (a GTK .xml file with a menu called "menu").

menu-actions.label: Menu commands
menu-actions.doc: The actions corresponding to the buttons of the menu.
menu-actions.description: For each menu entry, the command to run when you pick it.

expand.label: Fill empty space
expand.doc: Enables this module to consume all left over space dynamically.
expand.description: Stretch the module to use all the free space left in its section.
